newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb up on seed fundamentals, biotech.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb up on seed fundamentals, biotech.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp shares set another 52-week high of 58-3/4, up 1-3/4, on its strong fundamentals in the U.S. seed corn markets and enhanced value from its agricultural biotech portfolio, analysts said.
"If you look at the seed industry fundamentals with conventional hybrids, DeKalb has the momentum...," Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said.
He added that DeKalb, the second-place U.S. seed corn company behind Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc, has been gaining market share.

Dahlman added that DeKalb may also see an improved flow of royalties through Monsanto Co's planned purchase of Holden's Foundation Seeds, which makes germplasm -- or parent seed stock. Monsanto holds 10 percent of DeKalb's voting A shares and 45 percent of its non-voting, publicly traded B shares, for an aggregate stake of 40 percent.
DeKalb Chairman Bruce Bickner said recently that the Monsanto-Holden's deal "may even enhance our opportunities for additional royalty income."

DeKalb, like other agricultural firms, has developed genes that can be implanted in crops to fight off insects or withstand the use of certain herbicides. Through the Monsanto-Holden's deal, DeKalb's portfolio of genes may find an outlet through Holden's.
Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said the Monsanto-Holden's deal could result in improved synergies between Holden's and DeKalb.
